points.statement: A symbolic verifier validates each chosen action against temporal safety and efficiency constraints, executing valid ones and asking the actor to replan invalid ones.
points.quote: A rule-based symbolic verifier checks each action against LTL-based safety and efficiency constraints; valid actions are executed by a low-level planner, while invalid ones prompt the actor to replan.

points.statement: An actor chooses high-level actions from observations while a critic examines whole trajectories and proposes temporal constraints to prevent future unsafe or inefficient behavior.
points.quote: The actor selects high-level actions from natural language observations, while the critic analyzes full trajectories and proposes new LTL constraints that shield the actor from future unsafe or inefficient behavior.

points.statement: Combining language-model reasoning with formal-logic guarantees is the core advantage.
points.quote: Our setup combines the reasoning strengths of language models with the guarantees of formal logic.

points.statement: The architecture can handle both fixed hand-specified safety constraints and adaptive learned soft constraints that encourage long-term efficiency.
points.quote: The architecture supports both fixed, hand-specified safety constraints and adaptive, learned soft constraints that promote long-term efficiency.

points.statement: During online operation, the language-model actor chooses abstract high-level actions based on a complete state description.
points.quote: Online, the LLM actor selects high-level abstract actions from a full state description.
